notes.title: Drivers of Strategic Management
notes.content: Strategic management emerges due to dynamic environments, increased competition, higher management demands, and the need for clearer organizational direction.

notes.title: Strategic Management Definition
notes.content: Strategic management is a process of anticipating the future and taking actions to achieve desired organizational outcomes. It involves [[1775469610770]].

notes.title: Strategic Decision-Making
notes.content: Strategic management includes making key decisions about the long-term development of the organization. See [[1775469610769]].

notes.title: Importance of Strategic Management
notes.content: Strategic management is essential for effective organizational management; without it, management becomes incomplete and ineffective.

notes.title: Strategic Management Components
notes.content: Key components include mission formulation, goal setting, identifying alternatives, strategy selection, implementation, and evaluation. See [[1775469610773]] and [[1775469610774]].

notes.title: Mission in Strategy
notes.content: The mission defines the organization's purpose by answering "What is our business and what should it be?" and guides long-term direction. See [[1775469610772]].

notes.title: Strategic Goals
notes.content: Strategic goals must be defined at all levels and include both short-term and long-term objectives to ensure organizational success. See [[1775469610772]].

notes.title: Strategy Formulation
notes.content: Strategy formulation involves analyzing internal and external environments and creating action plans to achieve objectives. See [[1775469610776]].

notes.title: Environmental Analysis
notes.content: Effective strategies require understanding both internal and external organizational conditions. See [[1775469610775]].

notes.title: Resource Allocation in Strategy
notes.content: Strategy determines how resources are allocated to maximize opportunities and minimize threats.

notes.title: Levels of Strategy
notes.content: Strategies exist at multiple levels: organizational, functional (e.g., marketing, finance), and operational.

notes.title: Strategic Innovation and Growth
notes.content: Strategic actions include continuous innovation, identifying new opportunities, and strengthening competitive advantage.

notes.title: Situational Nature of Strategy
notes.content: Strategies must be tailored to specific organizational contexts; what works for one organization may not work for another.

notes.title: Strategy Implementation
notes.content: Strategy implementation requires organizational structure, budgeting, motivation systems, culture alignment, and leadership. See [[1775469610782]].

notes.title: Organizational Alignment
notes.content: Successful implementation requires all members to understand and execute their role in the strategic plan. See [[1775469610781]].
